sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: docs/guide/backends.md
sources.locator: Backend setup and auth environment variables
sources.finding: The first-party backend setup explicitly accepts user provider API credentials, including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY, as well as native CLI logins. Model usage is billed by the selected provider, separately from the free Ralph software.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: docs/installation.md
sources.locator: Prerequisites OS; installation methods
sources.finding: The first-party installation guide explicitly supports macOS, Linux and Windows for the native Ralph CLI. These are terminal clients rather than desktop GUI applications.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: crates/ralph-core/src/hatless_ralph.rs
sources.locator: HatlessRalph coordinator, HatInfo::event_publishing_guide and workflow_section; docs/guide/backends.md per-hat backends; event_loop/mod.rs
sources.finding: The product always supplies a Hatless Ralph coordinator role. Its shipped prompt instructs that coordinator to delegate through ralph emit events to named specialized hats, and event publishing starts a fresh iteration with clear context. Hats can select distinct coding-agent backends, publish results/events back into the product event loop and retain task/event state. This is product-supplied coordination, not merely display of provider-native subagents.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: backend/ralph-web-server/src/runner/ProcessSupervisor.ts
sources.locator: spawn detached and unref; api/server.ts host binding; README ralph web --legacy-node-api
sources.finding: The documented alpha web command can enable the legacy Node backend. That backend binds an operator-selected network host, starts detached native Ralph processes, persists PID/status/logs and can reconnect after server restarts. Agent work is owned by that server process tree rather than a browser connection. This is a self-hosted alpha mode; no managed Ralph cloud is supplied.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: backend/ralph-web-server/src/api/rest.ts
sources.locator: POST /api/v1/tasks autoExecute; serve.ts Dispatcher setup; runner/RalphTaskHandler.ts
sources.finding: The alpha legacy Node REST API is explicitly for external consumers. Creating an unblocked task auto-enqueues it unless autoExecute is false, and the product-owned Dispatcher executes it through RalphTaskHandler without a human click for each run. The backend service must remain running; no cron-schedule claim is established.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: crates/ralph-telegram/src/service.rs
sources.locator: Telegram update polling and MessageHandler::handle_message; handler.rs human.guidance and human.response
sources.finding: The Telegram integration routes incoming human messages to the selected loop. The polling service passes message text and chat ID to the handler, which appends human.guidance or human.response events to that loop; messages are not restricted to one sender identity in the inspected handler path. Distinct humans can send messages from their separate Telegram accounts (including a shared group chat) to steer the same loop; they do not share an ADE owner bearer credential. Per-human attribution and team permissions are not supplied by this path.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: crates/ralph-cli/src/loops.rs
sources.locator: Loop launch, diff and publish-review operations; core event loop; web backend routes and database schema
sources.finding: Bounded inspection of the native loop and alpha web runtime found installed host CLI processes and Git-worktree separation, without product-managed container/VM provisioning, enterprise human SSO or named human team permissions. Hat roles are agent operational roles. publish-review pushes a branch and writes a Markdown handoff; it does not create or manage a pull request.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: crates/ralph-core/src/diagnostics/mod.rs
sources.locator: DiagnosticsCollector::new and RALPH_DIAGNOSTICS environment flag
sources.finding: Ralph diagnostic collection is opt-in through RALPH_DIAGNOSTICS=1. When unset or another value, the collector creates no diagnostic directory or loggers. It controls local agent output, traces, hook-run telemetry and performance JSONL files; provider telemetry is separate.

sources.title: ralph-orchestrator: public preview availability
sources.locator: Web Dashboard (Alpha); ralph web --legacy-node-api opt-in; Development commands
sources.finding: The first-party README explicitly labels the web dashboard Alpha, warns of breaking changes, and documents ralph web --legacy-node-api as the opt-in deprecated Node backend. The unattended task-dispatch path and operator-server mode inspected in that backend are publicly enableable experimental paths.
